accuracy.evidence: The surprise/secret distinction (a surprise is happy and will be told soon; a secret that is scary, upsetting or must never be told should be shared with a trusted adult, even after a promise) matches NSPCC Talk PANTS guidance ('Speak up, someone can help'; use the word surprise, not secret, for happy things) and the PSHE Association Programme of Study (2020) KS1 keeping-safe content on good surprises versus secrets to share with a trusted adult. The DfE Relationships Education guidance (2019) supports knowing when it is right to break a confidence and how to report concerns. The warning phrases (special secret, threats of trouble or harm, 'nobody will believe you', gifts for silence) are the grooming and bullying tactics listed in NSPCC guidance. Nothing graphic is described: the only harm card says 'someone hurt me'. All arithmetic in the parameterised items checked at range corners (1+1 to 5+3, 2+1 to 4+3, 2 to 6, 2+1 to 5+3).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented confusions: a secret called 'special' must be good (the special-secret card is refused in Good surprise and the prediction offers 'Yes, it is special'), a present or sweets make it fine (prediction plus warning-word card and challenge), a surprise stays hidden for ever (the 'Never' box only accepts the worry card; a surprise dropped there is refused), a promise must be kept ('Keep the promise' is refused with 'you can break a promise to keep a worry secret'), telling a teddy, the asker or an online stranger counts (each refused with its own reason), and mixing excited feelings with worry (giggly and can't-wait chips refused).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagsecret is built on this topic's two tests: a week strip from Monday to Sunday plus a Never box where each surprise must land on the day it is told and only the worry secret fits Never; a feelings scene with Mia; a warning-words scene of speech bubbles; and a two-stage tell scene where the trusted person is chosen and then the promise dilemma is resolved. It is not 858 flagtrust (helping hand of trusted adults, lost in a shop, saying no to touch, one secrets sort) or the feelings labs 228 flagsoma and 398 flagbrain; the 6-token shingle gate reports no flag lab above 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers the rules by acting: the 'Not ever' card bounces off every day and only fits Never, so the time test is found, not told; tapping 'I feel giggly' is refused while 'My tummy feels sick' counts, so the feeling test is felt out; choosing Mum or the teacher leads to the promise question, and only 'Tell anyway' gets 'Thank you for telling me'. Each DONE line then states the rule.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 'Yes, it is special' for a special secret (refused in the sort), 'Yes, for ever' for how long a surprise stays hidden (every surprise has a day on the week strip), and 'Yes, I got a present' for sweets to keep quiet (the sweets bubble is one of the four warning signs). The reveal line names the right answer.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven questions; every wrong option maps to a named slip: 'soon' (it will be told soon, so it is a surprise), 'ever' (a surprise does not stay hidden for ever), 'special' (calling it special does not make it good; a grown-up should not ask you to keep secrets from Mum), 'feel' (if it makes you feel bad, do not keep it), 'sweets', 'promise', 'asker', 'teddy' and 'excited'. Clicked through with chal.cjs.

readability.evidence: Kid text is short sentences of one or two clauses with everyday words (present, party, scared, tummy), well inside the family kid limit; adult text names the PSHE, DfE and NSPCC basis and the safeguarding tactics in plain terms, inside the adult limit (validators pass). Canvas text is a short heading per scene and short cards.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs: what a surprise is; what a worry secret is plus the two tests; warning words; who to tell and that a promise does not stop you. Adult paragraphs: curriculum and safeguarding basis, the time and feeling tests and the tactics, named common mistakes, and what to do at home. The content gate finds no filler phrase.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px phone screenshots in light and dark for all five scenes: six sort cards in a 2 x 3 grid with 3-line text, the two bins with the icon left of the label and sorted names wrapping underneath (fixed after the first screenshot showed the gift icon overlapping the label), the week strip as two rows of four big day boxes, feeling chips in a 2 x 3 grid beside Mia, speech bubbles in a 2 x 3 grid, and six person tiles with labels in two rows.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: 'Surprise: Mum's cake' and 'Worry: Mum's cake' with full-text aria-labels, a day button for each of Monday to Sunday and Never ('Put Dad's card on Friday'), a button per feeling and per speech bubble, 'Tell my teacher' style buttons and 'Tell anyway' / 'Keep the promise'. The canvas aria-label carries each scene description and every piece of feedback; challenge feedback is a role=status live region; ✓, ✗ and ⚠ mark state as well as colour; axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) is clean in both themes.

PSHE Association (2020) Programme of Study for PSHE Education, Key stages 1 to 5: KS1 keeping safe
DfE (2019) Relationships Education, Relationships and Sex Education and Health Education: statutory guidance (being safe)
